questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would like to go somewhere with a different nature than what I was used to, and preferably a place where i could speak the mother language. That i why Bergen became my destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Do it if you would like to study in a different environment than you are used to, and would like to try out new things and routines outside of what you are used to from home.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Things went quite easy. However, the mobility online website is a bit confusing. It is also frustrating that it seems like Copenhagen University and the host university (in this case Bergen) didn't seem to "speak together". I had some trouble with my courses, and i had to have several separate mail correspondences with each of the universities, because no one seemed to have the responsibility..

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many of the information, you get on your mail from the host university. However, there were some confusion about the intro days. You had to seek out a lot of information by yourself. But the Studentcenter (studentsenteret) is very helpful if you have any questions!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The "freshers week" programme is not working. It is badly coordinated (at least at the faculty of humanities) and there is a great lack of activities without the main purpose being drinking alcohol. I managed to participate in the activities i felt like doing, but for people who find new social situations hard, I think the intro programme needs some rethinking.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I searched at
finn.no
and was super lucky to find a nice apartment, just 20-30 by foot from school.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Many of my friends lived at Fantoft. It is nice if you would like to be around other exchange students and have a very social every day life. However, i liked living in a smaller apartment with to other girls, as it was closer to downtown (took me 20.30 minutes to walk which I enjoyed a lot) and it felt a bit more like "home" :). But there is a lot of fun social activities going on at Fantoft!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I wished to register for courses taught in norwegian. They are not in the course list for exchange students in the "studentweb" website, so I had to email the faculties in which my courses were taught. That was a bit of a mess, and a lot of back and fourth emailing, but in the end, it all worked out, you just need a bit of patience.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UIB are very polite and helpfull. You just need a bit of patience, as the responding time can be a bit long, especially during summer- and christmas vacation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It all worked out in the end and i got the courses i wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're in doubt, send an email to UIB. They are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One of my courses, I felt like was below my level. The other one was similar to what I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had much fewer teaching hours than at UCPH. In one of my courses, seminars where student driven and not obligatory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: KVIK201 and KVIK102.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: KVIK201!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can do almost everything!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Spire" is a very nice and welcoming group of students that are the Bergen part of a Norwegian environmental and development organization. I would also recommend the wednesday hiking ( 7 fjell på 7 uker) organized by Sammen. If you like fishing, the BSI fishing club is also very very nice people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes! and sleep in a DNT hut! For hiking, i would recommend Gullfjellet and Hananipa. Fpr trips to DNT huts, I went to BT-hytta and Høgabu! So amazing, and a true norwegian experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Bergen is a very welcoming city and people are very nice. My experience is, that is is easiest to get in touch with other norwegians by joining one of the student clubs/activities.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join one of the student clubs/activities!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Norwegian people seem to have a friends group and sticks to it. But it's the same thing about danes I think. My best advice would be to attend to or engage in one of the student clubs or student activities. And there is plenty!!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Norwegian people really like to "hygge". Maybe even more than danes does!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open! Try out new things. This is a chance to try out something new for a couple of months. 
It is okay if it gets hard sometimes. You are away from home and maybe on your own. But most people are nice, and there is always something to do in Bergen! look out for the posters on the streets with activities, koncerts and so on. Be a volunteer in something, try out a new sport, check out "Sammen", they have A LOT of things going on. Meet new people and enjoy the nature. Go on trips! DNT is a fantastic opportunity.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When in doubt, go to the student center.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature. I really really enjoyed it and miss it a lot now.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home and people I love. But when i felt lonely, I searched for something to do outside the apartment, and I almost always got in a better mood. Meeting people, attending activities and being in the nature always helped.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
